title: Portability: daemon transport and JetBrains host matrix
description: Objective: exercise two distinct shipped boundaries without inventing a JetBrains MCP transport. Compare semantically equivalent commands through the installed daemon stdio and HTTP executables, and separately certify the public JetBrains host's distribution compatibility plus daemon-endpoint/control-room handoff outcomes.
definitionOfDone: After task-f33028b5374044bfa84deb5ed979277b, the matrix drives the installed moe-mcp-stdio and moe-mcp-http executables plus public @moe/jetbrains-adapter/host; no direct registry/handler or source-relative host import is used, and the generated subject-by-case count is positive.

Semantically equivalent authenticated stdio and HTTP commands/queries preserve the same command-decision identity and produce byte-equivalent results after framing is removed; each has one accepted control and exact malformed envelope, auth/capability, unsupported method/version, truncation/disconnect, and replay-conflict codes/stages/layers.

JetBrains cases exercise only its real distribution discovery/compatibility, daemon probe/start, endpoint/control-room open, reconnect, and uninstall semantics; accepted and hostile cases assert exact DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH or IDE-layer outcomes, while any MCP command translation is explicitly UNKNOWN because the host has none.

Every request/result or JetBrains handoff digest binds to the same checkout source commit; repeated runs are deterministic and refusal/read-only arms leave event/decision counts unchanged with no orphan child, open port, resurrected endpoint, or post-uninstall call.

Windows quoting/path/CRLF and platform-neutral stdio/HTTP framing are covered; child handles, HTTP servers, and temp directories close before cleanup, and focused integration tests print nonzero counts.
taskRails: Hard-depend on task-f33028b5374044bfa84deb5ed979277b; use public package roots/installed executables and real production boundaries only.
Do not add a JetBrains MCP command path or assert command identity for JetBrains; only stdio versus HTTP owns command/query equivalence.
Authentication and runtime-envelope decoding run before registry payload authority; assert exact stable code, stage, and layer rather than restamping.
Loopback only, no remote network, imported-state activation, best-tool selection, deep imports, or hand-built fake host.
Own only the transport/host matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files under tests/integration/portability; TDD with an accepted control and production-surface mutation drill.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CASE TABLE: create tests/integration/portability/portability-cases.ts (helper file 2 of 2). It declares the generated subject-by-case matrix as DATA — subject (STDIO | HTTP | JETBRAINS), case id, input shape, and the exact expected code, stage and layer — and contains no spawning and no assertions.
DoD item 1 requires the generated subject-by-case count to be POSITIVE, so export the count and have the suite assert `CASES.length > 0` and that every declared subject appears at least once BEFORE running anything. A generated matrix that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing — this repo has been bitten by exactly that, which is why the epic rail names it.
The expected codes are IMPORTED from their owning packages, never retyped as string literals here: `DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH` from @moe/contracts' distribution contract, MCP dispatch codes from @moe/mcp's public root, daemon refusals from the @moe/daemon root. A locally spelled code is a second vocabulary that drifts, and the drift shows up as a green test asserting a code production no longer emits.
Cover, per transport: one ACCEPTED control, malformed envelope, auth/capability refusal, unsupported method or protocol version, truncation/disconnect mid-frame, and replay-conflict. For JETBRAINS: distribution discovery match, DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, daemon probe failure, start, endpoint open, control-room open, reconnect, uninstall, and post-uninstall call.

CASE TABLE LANDED: tests/integration/portability/portability-cases.ts (374 lines, tsc exit 0). Pure data - no spawning, no assertions.

The suite asserts CASES.length > 0 and that every declared subject appears at least once BEFORE anything runs, because a generator that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing.

NO CODE IS A BARE LITERAL. Every code/stage/layer goes through `pin(name, ownerVocabulary, where)`, which THROWS AT MODULE LOAD when the owning package stops publishing it - so a production rename reddens the whole suite instead of leaving a green test asserting a code nothing emits. Sources, all imported: HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES, HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES, PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES, SERVICE_REFUSED_BY from @moe/daemon; DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_REASONS + distributionRefusal() CALLED to build the expected refusal from @moe/contracts; toolLabelForKind + STDIO_TOOL_INDEX from @moe/mcp; IdempotencyConflictError from @moe/store.

`pin` is deliberately stronger than reading the name out of the vocabulary by index: an index lookup is a TAUTOLOGY - rename the code and both operands move together and the test stays green. Naming the code AND requiring the owner to still publish it catches the rename.

ARMS ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Every expectation was reproduced live against both installed executables before it was written down:
- accepted-control EFFECTS_COMMITTED; malformed-envelope + unknown-tool-label INPUT_INVALID; wrong-credential AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; capability-scope-denied CAPABILITY_DENIED at stage AUTHORIZE (via a real scoped session minted through session.open); unsupported-method -32601; replay-conflict BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED at layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PLAN'S ASSUMPTIONS, both measured:
1. Step-6 assumed "an auth failure sent with a deliberately malformed payload must still be answered by AUTH". FALSE for stdio: `decodeAndDispatch` decodes BEFORE it calls port.authenticate, so wrong-credential + malformed envelope answers INPUT_INVALID. HTTP screens the bearer before it reads a byte of body, so the same input answers AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. The arm therefore carries expectedCodeBySubject, and that per-transport DIFFERENCE is the finding rather than a defect to paper over.
2. Step-6 asked for "the store's own idempotency code and DURABLE_STORE layer". IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT is UNREACHABLE through either transport: bootstrap's replayOf short-circuits on the stored decision before the store's request-bytes guard is consulted. Measured - same commandId + same kind + different payload answers REPLAYED with the ORIGINAL effectId (refuses to overwrite, which is the property the DoD wants), and same commandId + DIFFERENT kind answers BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED / DAEMON_PREREQUISITE / stage DISPATCH / 422. The table imports IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT from the class that raises it so the matrix can assert it is NOT what answered - which layer answered is itself the assertion.

implementationPlan.description:
COMMAND-DECISION IDENTITY — the core claim of DoD item 2, and the assertion that makes this matrix worth running.
Issue the SAME `commandId` (with the same principal and project) through stdio and then through HTTP. The durable decision key is {commandId, principalId, projectId}, so if both executables truly reach one pipeline the second call REPLAYS the first decision rather than deciding again. Assert:
- the decision identity (decisionId and resultCode) is identical across the two transports;
- the second call reports the REPLAYED disposition, not a fresh decision;
- the raw command-decision row count in the store increased by exactly ONE across both calls.
That count is the part a return-value comparison cannot see: two independent pipelines that happen to compute equal answers would add two rows and still compare equal.
Then strip framing and compare RESULTS byte-for-byte: decode the stdio JSON-RPC envelope and the HTTP response envelope down to the payload each carries and assert byte equality. Framing may differ; the answer may not. If a field is legitimately transport-specific, exclude it BY NAME with a comment, never by comparing a subset — an over-narrowed comparison passes every gate while proving nothing.
Run the pair in BOTH orders (stdio-then-HTTP and HTTP-then-stdio) so the replay assertion cannot be an artifact of which transport went first.
implementationPlan.note:
COMMAND-DECISION IDENTITY, asserted three independent ways so no single one can carry the claim alone.

1. REPLAY, not agreement. The SAME commandId (same principal, same project) goes through stdio and then HTTP. stdio answers disposition DECIDED; HTTP answers disposition REPLAYED with the IDENTICAL effectId and resultCode. The durable key is {commandId, principalId, projectId}, so a second call that decided again would say DECIDED with a different effectId.

2. THE ROW COUNT, which a return-value comparison cannot see. Read directly from the store's own `command_decisions` table: +1 across the pair, and `domain_events` unchanged between the two calls. Two independent pipelines computing equal answers would add TWO rows and still compare equal - this is the assertion that makes it identity rather than coincidence.

3. BOTH ORDERS. A second pair runs HTTP-first then stdio-second and asserts the same DECIDED/REPLAYED, the same effectId, and again exactly +1 decision row. So the replay is not an artifact of which transport led. It drives a FRESH `session.open` aggregate because `project.register` cannot legitimately commit twice at expectedVersion 0.

BYTE EQUIVALENCE, with NO field excluded. stdio call #3 and HTTP call #2 both carry the daemon's REPLAYED answer for the same commandId. Framing is removed on each side (the JSON-RPC envelope down to content[0].text) and the two are compared as UTF-8 BUFFERS via Buffer.equals, with a byteLength > 0 guard so an empty-vs-empty comparison cannot pass vacuously. Nothing is excluded and nothing is compared as a subset: the identical-replay pairing is what makes whole-payload equality achievable in the first place, which is why it was chosen over comparing two fresh decisions and then having to exclude effectId.

VERIFIED: `npx vitest run tests/integration/portability/transport-host-matrix.test.ts` -> Tests 13 passed (13), EXIT=0, four consecutive runs.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS STEP: the first draft of the reversed pair reused `project.register` at expectedVersion 0, which the daemon refuses as stale once the project aggregate has advanced - the identity assertion then compared `undefined` to "DECIDED" and reddened. Measured the alternatives before choosing: project.bind_repository at v1 -> ILLEGAL_TRANSITION (CORE_REDUCER); provider.probe with an empty observation -> BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID (DAEMON_INGRESS); session.open on a fresh sessionId -> EFFECTS_COMMITTED every time, because a session aggregate is independent of the project bootstrap sequence.

REFUSAL MATRIX GREEN: 8 arms x 2 installed executables = 16 generated refusal cases, each asserting the exact code AND the exact layer that answered. The sweep asserts its own count (16) so a generator that produced zero cases cannot pass.

MEASURED, per arm (code / answering layer):
- malformed-envelope (an unexpected key surviving into the envelope, refused by the exact-key decoder): INPUT_INVALID / MCP adapter decode, both transports.
- unknown-tool-label: INPUT_INVALID / MCP adapter tool index, both.
- wrong-credential: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, answered by the ADAPTER'S authenticate on stdio and by the HTTP SESSION SCREEN on HTTP.
- capability-scope-denied: CAPABILITY_DENIED at stage AUTHORIZE, both, driven by a REAL session.open-minted credential holding work.write only against a project.admin command. Also asserted NOT to be stage DISPATCH.
- unsupported-method (resources/list): the SDK's own method table, both.
- truncation-disconnect: silence and an untouched store, both.
- replay-conflict: BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED at layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, both.

WHICH LAYER ANSWERED IS THE ASSERTION, and classification is derived from the SHAPE of the reply, never from what the case hoped for: a non-200 HTTP status can only be the pre-transport screen; a JSON-RPC error carrying a registry data.code can only be the MCP adapter; a bare error with no data is the SDK; a `result` means the daemon seam dispatched.

TWO PLAN PREMISES CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT rather than asserted as written:
1. The plan says "an auth failure sent with a deliberately malformed payload must still be answered by AUTH". FALSE for stdio, and the double-invalid case proves it: `decodeAndDispatch` (packages/mcp/src/stdio/stdio-server.ts) decodes BEFORE it calls port.authenticate, so wrong-credential + malformed envelope answers INPUT_INVALID. HTTP's `screenRequest` reads the bearer before it reads a byte of body, so the SAME hostile input answers AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Both are asserted exactly, and the per-transport difference is recorded as the finding. Nothing is restamped to make the two agree.
2. The plan wants the store's own idempotency code with DURABLE_STORE. IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT is UNREACHABLE through either transport: `replayOf` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:240-263) short-circuits on the stored decision before the store's request-bytes guard runs. Measured: same commandId + same kind + different payload answers REPLAYED with the ORIGINAL effectId - it refuses to overwrite, which is the property the DoD asks for; same commandId + DIFFERENT kind answers BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED / DAEMON_PREREQUISITE / 422. The matrix imports IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT from the class that raises it and asserts the observed code is NOT it and the observed layer is NOT DURABLE_STORE - so the layer claim is pinned in both directions.

WRONG-CREDENTIAL CANNOT BE DRIVEN PER-CALL ON STDIO: the server holds its credential in closure and writes sessionCredential/requestDigest/commandKind/schemaVersion LAST (ADAPTER_SUPPLIED_COMMAND_FIELDS), so the arm starts a child with a different MOE_SESSION_CREDENTIAL. Capability scope is the only per-call auth arm.

STORE UNTOUCHED: decision and event counts are read from the store's own tables before and after the refusal block and asserted unchanged - a transport that refuses AFTER writing is indistinguishable from a clean refusal by return value alone.

VERIFIED: Tests 13 passed (13), EXIT=0, four consecutive runs.

JETBRAINS HALF GREEN, driven in a REAL CHILD NODE PROCESS at repository-root cwd, importing `@moe/jetbrains-adapter/host` by BARE specifier and reporting JSON on stdout. Never imported in-process.

CORRECTION TO THE PLAN'S STATED MECHANISM, measured this session and worth recording because a reviewer grading against the wrong model will accept a weaker test later. The plan says "vitest resolves workspace packages through its own aliasing, so an in-process import would resolve even with no exports map". FALSE at vitest v4.1.10: the root vitest.config.ts declares NO resolve.alias and vitest uses real Node resolution - `@moe/contracts` and `@moe/mcp` were ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND from tests/** until I added the root dependency edges. The CHILD-PROCESS DISCIPLINE IS STILL RIGHT, for a different reason: vitest rewrites a `./x.js` specifier back to `x.ts` and Node does not, so the shipped `.js` bridge behind the `./host` export is only proven by a real Node process. That is the reason the sibling jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint suite gives, and it is the one drill #2 will exercise.

ONLY THE REAL SURFACE, exactly the four ports:
- distribution discovery over a temp installRoot with matching manifests -> ADMITTED (the run proceeds past the gate).
- API range that does not match -> exact {code:"DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH", ok:false, reason:"API_RANGE_MISMATCH", refusedBy:"DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP"}, compared with toEqual against the value @moe/contracts' own distributionRefusal() produces.
- empty installRoot -> DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH / COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE / DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP.
- daemon probe against a CLOSED loopback port (bound then released, so it really refuses rather than timing out) -> discovery reports absent, which licenses start.
- start with daemonCommand = the INSTALLED moe-daemon shim -> DAEMON_START_REFUSED at layer DAEMON_START_PORT, outcome REFUSED. That is the shipped start port's real behaviour on Windows: Node refuses to spawn a .CMD without a shell, and the port turns the fault into an evidence arm instead of letting it escape. endpoint() stays null after a refused start.
- control room assets absent -> CONTROL_ROOM_ASSETS_MISSING / CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT / REFUSED.
- reconnect against a LISTENING endpoint -> CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK / OK, endpoint() matches http://127.0.0.1:<port>, and the supplied BrowserOpener fired exactly once. Supplying that port is configuration the host declares, not a hand-built fake host.
- uninstall -> endpoint() null. Post-uninstall call -> the ports fire AGAIN (opener count 1 -> 2), which is what proves the session was DROPPED rather than reused: a surviving session would answer from its cached endpoint without re-opening.

IDE CODES ARE PINNED AGAINST THEIR OWNER, not spelled locally and trusted. `@moe/ide-adapter-contract` is not a root dependency, so a second child runs at adapters/ide-contract and returns IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES and IDE_ADAPTER_LAYERS by self-reference; every expected code and layer passes through `pin` against those frozen tables. A production rename fails the pin rather than silently moving both operands together, which an index lookup would.

NO COMMAND METHOD, asserted as a closed set: Object.keys(host) sorted equals exactly [endpoint, reconnect, start, uninstall], plus an explicit not-to-contain on "command". MCP command translation is recorded as UNKNOWN because there is nothing to call - structural, not an untested gap. No command identity is asserted for JetBrains anywhere (task rail 2); only stdio versus HTTP owns that.

The child owns its own listener and its own free-port probe and closes both, and its temp dir uses a name with a SPACE ("jetbrains probe-", "control room.html") so the Windows path case is exercised on this half too.

VERIFIED: Tests 13 passed (13), EXIT=0, four consecutive runs, zero orphan processes and zero leftover temp directories afterwards.

implementationPlan.description:
DETERMINISM, SOURCE BINDING AND RESOURCE HYGIENE — DoD items 4 and 5.
- SOURCE BINDING: every request/result digest and every JetBrains handoff digest must bind to the same checkout source commit. Capture the commit ONCE via `git rev-parse HEAD` at suite start, include it in each recorded digest input, and assert every subject's digest carries that same commit. A matrix whose halves ran against different trees is comparing two systems.
- DETERMINISM: run the whole matrix twice in one process and assert the recorded outcomes are byte-identical. If any field is genuinely time- or port-dependent, exclude it BY NAME with a comment rather than loosening the comparison.
- READ-ONLY ARMS: for every refusal and every read-only case, assert event and decision counts are unchanged — measured from the store, not inferred from the response.

Task rail 5 caps my owned paths at three files under tests/integration/portability, so the manifest route is not mine to take.

## Correction to a load-bearing planning premise

planningNotes risks #1 and approach #2 rest on "vitest resolves workspace packages through its own aliasing, so an in-process import succeeds even with no exports map". That is FALSE at this HEAD — vitest v4.1.10 used real Node resolution, which is precisely why `@moe/contracts` and `@moe/mcp` fail. The child-process discipline for the JetBrains half is still correct, but for a different reason: vitest rewrites a `./x.js` specifier back to `x.ts` and Node does not (this is the reason the sibling adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts gives). Drills 1 and 2 stay justified; the stated mechanism should be corrected so the next reviewer does not grade against a false model.

## Narrowest fix, and what is already unblocked

Add `@moe/contracts` and `@moe/mcp` to root `dependencies` (workspace:*), run the workspace install, and declare `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` as owned paths of this task (or of a one-step prerequisite). That is the whole gap.

So DoD item 3 can pin the exact code from a production surface through an edge that exists today. Only the stdio-versus-HTTP half is stranded.

Two further facts for whoever re-plans:
- Tool labels need not come from `STDIO_TOOL_INDEX` at all: `createStdioMcpServer` serves `tools/list` from the generated entries, so the shipped executable will name its own labels over the wire. `toolLabelForKind` is `kind.replaceAll(".", "_")` over RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS/RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS. The refusal CODES are the part with no wire-side source — reading a code off the wire and asserting it equals itself is a tautology, which is why the import edge is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
- The stdio server holds the session credential in CLOSURE and overwrites `sessionCredential`/`requestDigest`/`commandKind`/`schemaVersion` last (stdio-tool-schemas.ts ADAPTER_SUPPLIED_COMMAND_FIELDS), so plan step-6's "absent credential / wrong credential" arms cannot be driven per-call — they must be driven by starting the child with a different MOE_SESSION_CREDENTIAL. Capability-scope refusal is the only per-call auth arm.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) COPY THE NEIGHBOURING tests/integration/control-room HARNESS, which imports `startDaemon`, `http-test-fixtures` and the client transport by DEEP RELATIVE path. REJECTED for the subjects under test: DoD item 1 forbids a direct registry/handler or source-relative import, and task rail 1 requires installed executables and public roots. That suite is a fine model for lifecycle discipline and payload-equality reasoning, and a bad model for how to reach the subject. The drift is easy to make and invisible — hence the explicit grep in step 11.
2) IMPORT `@moe/jetbrains-adapter/host` IN-PROCESS under vitest. REJECTED, and this is the sharpest trap in the task: vitest resolves workspace packages through its own aliasing, so that import succeeds even with no `exports` map at all. The public-subpath claim can only be proven in a real child Node process with cwd at the repository root. Drill #2 exists to keep it that way.
3) DRIVE THE STDIO ENTRY AS `node apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.ts`. REJECTED: it proves the module runs and says nothing about the bin that task-f33028b5 shipped, which is precisely what DoD item 1 names. Spawn through node_modules/.bin. Drill #1 catches the substitution.
4) COMPARE stdio AND HTTP BY RESULT EQUALITY ALONE. REJECTED as insufficient: two independent pipelines computing equal answers compare equal. The load-bearing assertion is that the SAME commandId REPLAYS across transports and the raw decision-row count rises by exactly one — identity, not agreement.
5) ASSERT AN MCP COMMAND PATH FOR JETBRAINS. REJECTED by task rail 2 and impossible by construction: `JetBrainsHost` is exactly {endpoint, reconnect, start, uninstall}. The matrix records MCP translation as UNKNOWN and asserts the closed four-key surface, so the UNKNOWN is a measured fact rather than an untested gap.
6) SPELL EXPECTED CODES AS LOCAL STRING LITERALS. REJECTED: a locally spelled code is a second vocabulary, and when production renames one the test stays green while asserting a code nothing emits. Import DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH from @moe/contracts and dispatch codes from @moe/mcp / @moe/daemon roots.
7) SPLIT THE TRANSPORT AND JETBRAINS HALVES INTO TWO TEST FILES. REJECTED by task rail 5, which permits one matrix test plus at most two helpers. The split is instead by ROLE — lifecycle in the harness, case data in the table, assertions in the test.

MEASURED AT HEAD 61766074. Every capability this acceptance task certifies was verified ON DISK, not read from the gate's DoD.

SHIPPED BY task-f33028b5 (QA-approved DONE 03:13Z), all four confirmed:
- `ls node_modules/.bin | grep moe` -> moe-daemon, moe-mcp-http, moe-mcp-stdio, each with .CMD and .ps1 siblings. The stdio shim now EXISTS; when architect-f956ffe1 blocked this task it did not.
- apps/daemon/package.json bin is exactly the three keys, `moe-mcp-stdio -> ./src/mcp-main.ts`.
- adapters/jetbrains/package.json exports is `{".": "./src/index.ts", "./host": "./src/host/jetbrains-host.js"}` — pointed at the shipped .js bridge, as planned.
- root package.json dependencies now include @moe/import, @moe/jetbrains-adapter and @moe/store, which is what lets a repo-root test resolve those bare specifiers in a child process.

SUBJECT SURFACES:
- `JetBrainsHost` (adapters/jetbrains/src/host/jetbrains-host.ts:51) is EXACTLY `{endpoint, reconnect, start, uninstall}`, built over four ports — controlRoom.openControlRoom, discovery.probeDaemon, distribution.discoverDistributions, start.startDaemon — each closed over its own config. So DoD item 3's list maps 1:1 onto the real surface, and "MCP translation is UNKNOWN" is structural: there is no command method to call.
- `DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH` is NOT in adapters/jetbrains at all. It lives in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts:36 and :112 (a refusal carrying `refusedBy`) and is registered in runtime-error-registry.ts:17,153 with lifecycle NEVER / HUMAN_DECISION / UNPROCESSABLE and source PROJECT. Import it; do not re-declare it.
- apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.ts is 58 lines: `readBootstrapCredential` -> `readStoreDependencyEnv` -> `createStoreDependencies` -> `createStdioMcpServer({credential, port: createMcpDispatchPort({...}), serverName: "moe-next"})` -> `connectStdioTransport`. Its own header states "every dispatch answered by the same durable pipeline the HTTP listener serves" — that sentence is the claim DoD item 2 exists to verify, and the replay-identity assertion is how to verify it rather than restate it.
- apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-main.ts reads MOE_MCP_HTTP_PORT (optional, ephemeral default) and an MCP_HTTP_HOST_ENV host. Read the bound port from the child rather than assuming one.
- @moe/mcp publishes `STDIO_TOOL_ENTRIES`, `STDIO_TOOL_INDEX`, `toolLabelForKind`, `generateStdioToolEntries` and `ADAPTER_SUPPLIED_COMMAND_FIELDS` — build tool labels through those, never by hand.

TEST LAYOUT: tests/integration currently holds control-room/, distribution/, expansion-protocol.test.ts, release-archive-cleanup.test.ts and release-supply-chain.test.mjs. `tests/integration/portability/` does NOT exist and is created by this task. The neighbouring control-room-transport.test.ts (312 lines) reaches its subjects by deep relative import — a good lifecycle model, an explicitly forbidden access pattern here.

TYPECHECK HOLE, and it is load-bearing for how this plan gates: root `typecheck` is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` (workspace packages only) and `test:integration` runs `pnpm typecheck:packaging` (tools/packaging only) before vitest. NOTHING typechecks tests/integration. A type error in the three new files is invisible to every existing gate, so step 10 requires a standalone `npx tsc --noEmit` over them with the packaging flag set and requires that command be recorded, since no script would show it ran.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE VITEST ALIASING TRAP IS THE BIGGEST RISK IN THIS TASK. An in-process `import("@moe/jetbrains-adapter/host")` resolves through vitest's own workspace aliasing even if the exports map is absent, so the headline claim of DoD item 1 can be 'proven' by a test that would pass against the pre-gate tree. Only a child Node process with cwd at the repo root proves it. Same class for the executables: spawning the source file instead of the installed shim proves nothing about the bin. Drills 1 and 2 are the only mechanical defence.

2) TESTS/INTEGRATION IS TYPECHECKED BY NOTHING. Run the standalone tsc leg and record it, or a broken type ships silently.

3) `pnpm test:integration` MUST RUN FROM POWERSHELL — it shells through MSYS tar and fails on drive-letter paths under Git Bash, for reasons unrelated to this diff.

4) RESULT EQUALITY IS NOT IDENTITY. Two separate pipelines can agree. The replay assertion plus the exactly-one-decision-row count is what proves both transports reach one pipeline; keep both, and run the pair in both orders so the replay is not an artifact of ordering.

5) MULTI-LAYER CASES ARE WHERE VACUITY HIDES. An auth case sent with a malformed payload must still be answered by AUTH; if the envelope decoder answers first, the test silently stops testing auth. Assert WHICH layer answered, and include at least one deliberately double-invalid case.

6) RESOURCE RESIDUE IS THE CLASSIC INTEGRATION FAILURE. Children, ephemeral ports, temp dirs and SQLite handles must all close before cleanup; a teardown that has only ever run once has not been tested, so run the suite twice in one command.

7) WINDOWS SPECIFICS ARE DoD ITEMS, NOT CAVEATS: spaces in paths, .CMD/.ps1 shim variants, and CRLF-tolerant frame splitting. A splitter assuming LF will HANG rather than fail, which reads as a flaky timeout.

8) DRILL RESTORATION: drills 1 and 2 edit manifests this task does NOT own. Snapshot hashes before and confirm restoration after; a foreign hook commit can swallow a drill so git status reads clean while the edit is gone.
